name: The Soft Machines
description: A low-budget independent neural-feed feature about two synthetic-tissue laborers who fall into an unexpected partnership while working a night shift in a Tier 2 bio-processing facility, slowly uncovering evidence that their workplace is running unauthorized psychological trials on the workforce. The feed was produced on a shoestring by a three-person collective using unlicensed neural-scripting tools, giving the immersion a raw, slightly unstable quality that critics called 'authentically disorienting.' It circulated through Tier 2 mesh networks for two years before receiving a limited licensed release.
cultural_impact: The film's depiction of workplace psychological manipulation resonated so strongly with Tier 2 workers that 'soft machine' became slang for anyone who suspects their employer is running behavioral trials on them.
story_hooks: The unlicensed neural-scripting tools used to make the film are still active somewhere — and contain raw, unprocessed recordings of the crew's own emotional states during production.
The 'fictional' psychological trial depicted in the film appears to match the methodology of a real program documented in a leaked corporate memo from the same year.
One of the collective's three members is now a licensed Vantablack Media director — and refuses to discuss the film.
